item: Row 403: a keys folder that cannot be opened reads as an unreadable key, never an error and never no key
summary: is_this_installations_key and signing_key_state tested the key file with Path.exists(), which on Python 3.13 swallows only a missing path: on a keys folder without search permission (EACCES) it raised PermissionError where both promise an answer (reproduced as a non-root user, folder mode 000). The callers that reach it without own= got the raw error: the R795 passphrase check in a stream restore (stream_backup._why_the_volume_list_is_not_ours) stopped on an OSError instead of its own-key-unreadable reason, the row 339 step in merge_side_files raised instead of withholding the trust flags, and the export review (signing_key_state) raised instead of answering unreadable. A new _key_file_state does one os.stat: FileNotFoundError or NotADirectoryError is absent (False, none), any other failure to look is unreadable (None, unreadable), so a key whose state cannot be read is never this installation's own and never no key; a key file that is there but cannot be read already reads as None through existing_public_key_hex. The custody callers pass own= and were unaffected. No wording change, no new strings; what is accepted or refused is unchanged (R795, row 339).
